name: serializers/__init__.py
summary: Package-level facade that re-exports query serializers to provide a unified public API for the serializers module.
purpose: Simplifies imports for consumers by exposing key serializer classes at the package level, decoupling callers from the internal file structure of the serializers directory and reducing import verbosity.
responsibilities: Re-export QueryRequestSerializer from the query_request submodule
Re-export FeedbackSerializer and QueryHistorySerializer from the query_response submodule
Define the public API surface of the serializers package
Shield consumers from internal module reorganization
outputs: Unified package-level import interface for query-related serializers
architecture_notes: Implements a lightweight Facade pattern to aggregate the package's public interface. This is a standard Python packaging convention that improves developer ergonomics by allowing consumers to import all query serializers from a single entry point. It introduces a thin abstraction layer over the internal module layout, though it carries a risk of circular imports if submodules attempt to import from the package root.
improvements: Define an explicit __all__ list to control the public API and prevent namespace leakage
Use explicit re-export syntax (e.g., 'from .x import Y as Y') to ensure type checkers like mypy recognize the symbols as re-exported
Evaluate whether all serializers should be exposed at the package level or only the most commonly used ones to keep the API surface minimal
Add a module-level docstring explaining the intended import patterns for consumers
